findings.title: CF failures during source re-selection escape the item-resume result handling
findings.description: Re-evaluating the source can call `ContextForgeClient.list_tasks()` and `list_slices()`, which raise `ContextForgeError` or `ContextForgeNotAvailable` when `cf` fails. `resume_item()` handles `_Stop`, `GitEnvironmentError`, and `OSError`, but not these CF exceptions; the CLI also does not translate them. A transient CF failure therefore escapes as an unhandled exception instead of producing a clear, observable item-resume outcome and documented exit code. Handle and log these expected integration failures at the resume boundary.

findings.title: Mutating fan-out inner steps can bypass the project run lock
findings.description: `_step_mutates()` descends through `config["steps"]` but not `config["inner"]`. Fan-out accepts any single inner step other than another fan-out, and the executor runs that inner step; consequently, a fan-out with a mutating inner step such as `branch` can be classified as non-mutating and run without the lock. Inspect fan-out’s `inner` configuration when determining mutation, or reject mutating inner step types during validation.

findings.title: The new run-lock concurrency path lacks a required load test
findings.description: The added tests verify lock contention, process-exit release, and independent worktrees, but the new concurrency path has no load test exercising concurrent realistic run attempts with latency or resource bounds. The Python testing rules require a load test for concurrency paths. Add one that exercises competing mutating runs and gate it in CI.
